subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Zero's Revolutionary Birth
description: A micro-lesson that makes Zero's Revolutionary Birth usable.

hook.text: Zero didn't exist in Western math until the 12th century. India invented it. The concept of nothing changed everything.

buildup.text: Indian mathematician Brahmagupta defined zero around 628 CE. Arab scholars carried it to Europe via trade routes.

discovery.text: Zero enabled place-value systems. Without it, you can't write 10, 100, or calculate calculus. Math was unlocked.

twist.text: The Church resisted zero because nothingness implied the void—a concept that threatened creation theology.

climax.text: A concept the West feared became the foundation of modern mathematics. Nothing turned out to be everything.

quiz.question: Who first defined the concept of zero mathematically?
